C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL.Summary: Add the bundled managed skill vvoc-project-session-history — the project-session recap extractor that reads OpenCode's local SQLite history (V2 session_v2/session_message with a legacy V1 session/message+part fallback) — and extend the managed-skill delivery machinery with a scripts/ subdirectory capability so executable skill files install, sync, and drift-check alongside SKILL.md and references/ with the same conservative semantics. The extractor script ships byte-identically to the V2-aware direct fix of 2026-11-25, while SKILL.md is restructured into the canonical six-block skill grammar; user-installed legacy standalone copies are never touched and are removed manually.
C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL.Problem: The project-session recap capability ("что мы делали в этом проекте?", stopping-point recovery, handoff from recent sessions) currently exists only as a hand-installed standalone skill directory at ~/.config/opencode/skills/project-session-history, maintained by manual md5 comparison across machines. It is invisible to the bundle: not in templates/skills/, not in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES, not covered by install/sync, tests, README, or the managed-skill compatibility surface, so vvoc sync cannot deliver it and no deterministic gate protects it. Its extractor was repaired on 2026-11-25 as a direct fix (V2 session_v2 session list with V1 fallback, reasoning/tool part exclusion, slug title fallback) with no bundled home for the result. The managed-skill delivery path is also structurally insufficient for this skill: install/sync knows only SKILL.md and references/, no managed skill today ships an executable script, and the standalone SKILL.md is plain markdown that does not conform to the canonical six-block grammar the grammar gate enforces on every shipped template.

Goals.Goal: Ship templates/skills/vvoc-project-session-history/SKILL.md and templates/skills/vvoc-project-session-history/scripts/project_history.py. The script is byte-identical to the fixed standalone version of 2026-11-25; SKILL.md is restructured into the canonical six-block skill grammar (required scope/workflow/rules/done blocks in canonical order), with the frontmatter name equal to the directory name and a single-line description of at most 1024 characters carrying explicit trigger branches and exclusions.
Register "vvoc-project-session-history" in MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES, joining the stable managed-skill compatibility surface.

Extend managed-skill delivery with a scripts/ capability mirroring the references/ placement exactly: template-side listing and loading of script files one level deep under templates/skills/<name>/scripts/, and install/sync copying to <managedSkillsDir>/<name>/scripts/ by pure template content comparison (create/keep/update). Script files carry no per-file ownership marker and no script-level frontmatter guard: they are written only when the parent SKILL.md was not skipped, exactly like references.
Extend the managed-skill staleness inspection to scripts: installed script files are compared against their templates with the same warning shape as SKILL.md and references drift.
Leave the eleven existing managed skills and every write result they produce unchanged: they have no scripts/ directory, so their install/sync output is identical before and after this change.
Update the managed-skill count arithmetic in src/lib/opencode.test.ts and the literal totals stated in the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification scenario to the new deterministic values.

Document the skill in README: a row in the managed-skills table with accurate family framing, an additive entry for the new name in the managed-skill compatibility-surface list of the Stability and compatibility section, and a note that pre-bundle standalone copies of project-session-history are user-owned and removed manually after the first sync.

Constraints.Constraint: The extractor script is transferred without logic changes: the session-list UNION with explicit column list, dual legacy+modern message reading with deduplication, typed non-text part exclusion, slug title fallback, and read-only database access (mode=ro, query_only) are frozen as shipped behavior. Byte-identity applies to the script only; SKILL.md is restructured, not transferred verbatim.

scripts/ delivery mirrors the references/ contract: one level deep, text files, template content as the comparison source, no deletion of unknown installed files, no per-file ownership marker, and writes gated only by the parent skill's skip state. A user-edited installed script under a non-skipped parent is refreshed to the template, exactly like a reference.
Config safety is unchanged: writes stay inside vvoc-owned directories; no detection, migration, or removal of the legacy standalone project-session-history skill on any machine.
The script stays Python 3 executed via python3; the skill documents that requirement; there is no Bun/TypeScript rewrite and no runtime probing of the interpreter during install.
The skill remains read-only toward the database and the repository; its guidance keeps treating session history as historical evidence requiring fresh Git checks.

SKILL.md keeps a self-sufficient core inside the six-block grammar, retains the Data Source Layout content (session_v2 with V1 fallback, dual message stores, text-only parts, immediate V2 writes and the resulting --skip-newest semantics) as markdown inside the allowed blocks, instructs running python3 on scripts/project_history.py relative to the skill's own directory with no absolute or legacy standalone path, and names only files, commands, and paths that exist after installation; the template names no references/ paths, so the reference-contract grammar check passes trivially.
README, the M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS and M-CLI-CONFIG graph projections, and the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification projection are reconciled inside the approved change lifecycle, not retroactively.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No changes to extractor behavior, message selection, deduplication, output format, or CLI flags — the 2026-11-25 direct fix is the frozen source, and no retroactive C-* bundle is created for it.
No auto-migration, detection, or removal of legacy standalone project-session-history copies; interim routing duplication until manual removal is accepted.
No scripts/ capability for managed agents, no support for arbitrary directory trees, nested paths, or binary assets — scripts/ is a flat sibling of references/ only.
No rewrite of project_history.py into TypeScript or Bun, no vendoring of the extractor into other vvoc tools, and no new Python dependencies.
No changes to unrelated managed skills, plugins, the config schema, managed agents, the workflow engine, or release automation.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES contains "vvoc-project-session-history", and loading its template returns SKILL.md whose YAML frontmatter name equals the directory name with a single-line description of at most 1024 characters.

AC-02: templates/skills/vvoc-project-session-history/scripts/project_history.py exists and carries the literal content markers of the frozen fix: "UNION ALL", the column list "id, project_id, parent_id, slug, directory, title, time_updated", the failure message "database has neither session nor session_v2 table", the typed non-text part exclusion guard in content_text, and the slug title fallback expression.
AC-03: The template-side script API lists and loads scripts/ files one level deep for the new skill and returns an empty list for every skill without a scripts/ directory.

AC-04: install and sync copy the script by pure template content comparison (create when absent, keep when identical, update when different): install writes scripts/ when it creates the skill or runs with force, mirroring the references/ placement in the install loop; sync writes scripts/ whenever the parent skill is not skipped; a user-edited installed script under a non-skipped parent is updated back to the template; and no per-file frontmatter or ownership check is applied to script files.

AC-05: The existing managed-skill and opencode test expectations covering the eleven pre-existing skills pass unchanged, apart from count arithmetic that includes the new skill's entries, demonstrating their install/sync write results are unaffected.

AC-06: expectedManagedSkillResultCount in src/lib/opencode.test.ts counts one SKILL.md plus references plus scripts per skill, its skipped-skill subtraction drops references and scripts, the install path-shape assertion accepts scripts/ paths, and the literal totals in the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS scenario become 35 files (33 in the vv-spec-skip case).

AC-07: The SKILL.md frontmatter description carries explicit trigger branches (project recap, "что мы делали в этом проекте", stopping-point and context recovery) and explicit exclusions (token usage, cache, and cost analysis belong to vvoc-usage-analytics; current repository state requires fresh Git checks, not history).

AC-08: SKILL.md conforms to the canonical six-block grammar — required scope, workflow, rules, and done blocks in canonical order from the block allowlist — with the Data Source Layout and extractor-options content as markdown inside the allowed blocks, and the run instruction python3 scripts/project_history.py relative to the skill's own directory with no absolute or legacy standalone path.

AC-09: README gains the vvoc-project-session-history row in the managed-skills table with correct family framing, an additive entry for the name in the managed-skill compatibility-surface list of the Stability and compatibility section, and a statement that standalone pre-bundle copies are user-owned and removed manually after the first sync.

AC-10: The managed-skill staleness inspection reports installed scripts/ files that differ from their templates with the same warning shape as SKILL.md and references drift, and reports nothing for skills without scripts.
AC-11: bun run check, bun run build, and bun run pack:check pass, and the packed archive contains templates/skills/vvoc-project-session-history/SKILL.md and scripts/project_history.py.

AC-12: The M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS and M-CLI-CONFIG graph modules and the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification entry remain truthful for the new skill and the scripts/ capability, reconciled within this change's lifecycle.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: manual: python3 <installed managed skills dir>/vvoc-project-session-history/scripts/project_history.py --project <a real project> --sessions 3
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Delivery, grammar, and content-marker tests demonstrate registration, six-block grammar conformance, template loading, scripts/ listing/loading, install/sync create-keep-update semantics gated by the parent skill, the updated count arithmetic and path-shape acceptance, and unchanged expectations for existing skills. The staleness inspection reports script drift with the reference-shaped warning. pack:check shows both skill files inside the packed archive. The manual smoke run against a real OpenCode database returns recent sessions and is recorded as change-time evidence, not a CI gate; deterministic tests assert delivery, not extractor model behavior.

Assumptions.Assumption: The shipped script is byte-identical to the fixed standalone version of 2026-11-25 (md5 09a533b18b7ed4794de118d2041b9fc4); any byte difference is out of scope and requires amending this spec.
python3 exists on machines where the skill is invoked; the skill documents the requirement and install does not probe for it.
The name vvoc-project-session-history joins the stable managed-skill surface; renaming it later is a documented breaking change.

Legacy standalone copies of project-session-history are removed manually by the user on each machine after the first sync that delivers the bundled skill; interim duplication in skill routing is accepted and not treated as a defect of this change.
The empty references/ and assets/ directories of the standalone skill are not transferred; only SKILL.md and scripts/project_history.py ship.

The new literal totals in AC-06 (35 and 33) are derived from the current reference counts (22 references across eleven skills, vv-spec contributing 2) plus one new SKILL.md and one script; the implementing plan re-derives them from the test helper at execution time and amends the spec if the arithmetic differs.

This stage delivers a draft specification and explanatory design context only; approval and a GraceChangePlan precede any source change, and no implementation, commit, installation, or release happens as part of specification authoring.
